title: DR1 saves a document the user has filled in but not yet added when they press Save and continue, stopping them if it is incomplete; the frontend's Continue throws the part-filled row away without a word.

finding.frontend: The page has two ways forward and only one of them looks at the form. Save and add another validates the row and saves it. Continue does not read the form fields at all — the post handler falls past the add branch, checks only whether any already-saved document is still being scanned, and redirects (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:255-279). A user who types a reference, picks a date, chooses a file and then presses Continue rather than Save and add another loses all three and is not told. Nothing on the page distinguishes the two buttons' effect on the row in front of the user.
finding.prototype: Both exits look at the row. Save and add another validates every field and re-renders with errors if any is missing — dr1-upload-documents-error is that state, listing "Enter a document reference", "Select a document type", "Enter a date of issue" and "Upload a document". Save and continue applies the same validation, but only once the user has chosen a document type, treating that as the signal that a row is in progress; if the rest of the row is incomplete the user is held on the page with the same messages (dr1-upload-documents-continue-error, showing the three remaining errors with the type already chosen), and if it is complete the row is saved on the way out (app/routes.js:10173-10192). Pressing Save and continue on a completely untouched row moves on, because uploads are optional.
finding.difference: Make Continue read the in-progress row rather than ignore it: if any of reference, type, date or file has been filled in, validate the whole row and hold the user on the page with the same messages Save and add another produces; if it validates, save it before moving on. DR1 uses the document type as the has-the-user-started signal, so this depends on the document-type field existing; until it does, the equivalent signal is any of the three fields being non-empty. The existing scan-settling block on Continue is a frontend extra and stays.
finding.falsifiedBy: Filling in a reference, a date and a file on the frontend, pressing Continue, and finding the document in the saved list or being held on the page.
finding.correction: The silent-discard claim is confirmed, and the mechanism is exactly as written: the Continue button posts action=continue (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/template.njk:92), which is neither the add branch nor a remove action, so the handler falls through to the settling check and redirects without ever touching payload.accompanyingDocumentReference, the date or the multipart file (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/controller.js:255-279). Nothing client-side saves it either — the only submit listener on the form is the oversize check (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/documents/client/oversize-validation/submit.js:45-57), which returns without acting when the file is within the limit. What is overstated is the illustration and the proposed rule. DR1's soft validation is keyed on the document type alone: the branch is entered only when the posted documentType is a valid option (app/routes.js:10173-10192), so a DR1 user who fills in a reference, a date and an attachment but leaves the select on "Select one" and presses Save and continue is ALSO carried forward with the row silently dropped. The scenario in finding.frontend — reference, date and file with no type — is therefore not a parity difference at all; the difference only exists once a type has been chosen. The consequence is that finding.difference proposes behaviour stricter than DR1 asks for: DR1 does not treat any-field-non-empty as the in-progress signal, only a chosen type, and the interim rule offered here should be recorded as an extrapolation rather than as DR1's requirement. falsifiedBy has the same problem — it tests the frontend but not the gap. Slots left as written; the finding stands, narrowed.

relatedTo.why: DR1 keys the Save and continue validation on a chosen document type, which the frontend has no field for
